video_caption: The video opens on a teal background with a white circular icon featuring a red cross, labeled "Healthcare". This is quickly joined by a second white circle with an atom icon and "Education", then a third with a storm cloud icon and "Environment". A fourth white circle containing a parachute and a red cross symbol appears next, labeled "International aid", and finally, a fifth white circle with a scales of justice icon, labeled "Crime", slots into the sequence. Below these five icons, white text reads: "Issues affecting all our lives are shaped and driven by Parliament." The icons and text then slide off-screen to the left as the background abruptly changes to a solid magenta. In the center of the screen, the white text "But how" appears, followed by "did it all begin?", with a thin grey line underneath.

The video segment opens with a static shot featuring a white symbol in the center of the frame, set against a solid grey background. The symbol is a crown positioned directly above a portcullis-like grid pattern, all enclosed within a vibrant green circular badge.

The video segment opens with a split screen, featuring a teal background on the left and a light blue on the right, with two speech bubbles: a black one on the lower left containing the white text "10 Downing St" and a yellow one on the upper right with a brown crown icon. The screen then transitions to a yellow background, where a pink rectangular block appears, filled with numerous small, white, stylized human figures, labeled "MPs and Peers" in black text above it. Below this, a longer turquoise block, also filled with similar white figures, appears, with the white text "Support staff" in its center, signifying the roles of Members of Parliament/Peers and their support staff. The scene then shifts to a vibrant lime green background, as a yellow ribbon-like graphic with pink text appears, twisting to reveal the message: "HOLDING GOVERNMENT TO ACCOUNT". Following this, a teal background displays three circles of varying sizes: a small dark grey circle labeled "Government", a slightly larger pink circle labeled "Parliament" to its right, and a much larger yellow circle expanding from the right, labeled "The Public", illustrating the relative scale and accountability. The scene then changes to show two stylized parliament chambers, one with red seats on the left and another with green seats on the right, initially empty. As people appear seated in both chambers, a diverse group of flat-design individuals, some in suits, some in more casual attire, including one person in a wheelchair, fill the seats. Speech bubbles emerge from various individuals, displaying questions such as "How?", "What?", "Who?", "Where?", "Why?", and "Explain?", highlighting the questioning and challenging role of Parliament. Close-up shots further emphasize these questions, showing individuals with speech bubbles asking "Explain?", "What?", and "Why?".

The video begins with an animated man in a grey suit, black hair, and dark skin, smiling in front of a plain yellow background. He is soon joined by four other diverse animated figures, forming a row of five individuals—three men and two women—of varying ethnicities and hair colors, all wearing business attire and smiling, seated behind a brown table with documents in front of them. The scene then transitions to a grey background where a large yellow circle appears, displacing the previous figures to the right. Inside the circle, numerous small, diverse animated figures stand around the central word "Policy." A red banner with the text "Select Committee" (English translation) is pinned to the top left, connected to the circle by a dotted line. The video returns to the five seated figures, now on a light grey background, with thought bubbles above them containing a thumbs-up, a lightbulb, and question marks ("???"). Two additional animated figures appear, one on the left in a white lab coat and glasses, and one on the right in a blue suit with medals, with speech bubbles above them reading "Knowledge" and "Experience" (English translation), respectively. More diverse animated figures then join the scene, standing on either side of the table, and two new speech bubbles appear, reading "View" and "Opinion" (English translation). The scene cuts to a purple background with a red circle, inside which a white document titled "Report" is displayed. Finally, the video transitions to a teal background where a yellow ribbon unfurls, displaying the text "MAKING LAWS" (English translation).

The video begins with a static image featuring a flag-like design, diagonally split with a red top-right section and a green bottom-left section. Centered on this background is a white stylized Portcullis emblem, a parliamentary symbol, surmounted by a crown. This transitions to a solid bright yellow background with a white circle in the center containing a blue question mark with a grey middle section and a light blue dot. The background then changes to a solid teal color, and the question mark inside the white circle becomes uniformly light blue. Subsequently, the question mark disappears, replaced by a white stack of documents within the circle, and the word "Bill" appears in white text below it. Finally, five additional circular icons animate and arrange themselves in a pentagon shape around the central "Bill" icon: a light blue circle with colorful stick figures labeled "Opposition parties," a dark grey circle with the number "10" labeled "Governing parties," a red megaphone icon labeled "Campaign groups," a purple circle with a man in a tie labeled "Civil servants," and a red circle with three diverse-looking people labeled "Public inquiries."

The video segment illustrates a policy-making process through animated icons and text on a light beige background, with a continuous pink timeline at the bottom that moves a small pink circle to indicate progress. Initially, a light green icon of two stacked documents with the text "Green paper" (English) is displayed inside an orange circle, representing a preliminary government report discussing policy options. This transitions to an orange circle containing three stylized head-and-shoulder icons of people (one with blonde hair and a red top, one with dark skin, dark hair, and a purple top, and one with dark hair and a grey top, all smiling) with the text "Public discussion and consultation" (English), symbolizing the public debate phase. Next, the scene changes to an orange circle with two stacked documents, the top one white with blue lines of text, labeled "White paper is published" (English), indicating a more formal and detailed policy plan. Finally, the white paper icon is replaced by a circular icon split into teal and lime green halves, showing two brown hands with cuffs; one thumb is pointing down on the teal side, and the other is pointing up on the green side, accompanied by the text "Vote on proposal" (English), signifying the decision-making stage where the proposal is voted on.

The video segment illustrates a step-by-step process using animated graphics and text. From 0:00 to 0:01, a light-beige background features a pink horizontal timeline with a white circular marker moving along it. Above the timeline, a circular graphic is displayed, split vertically into blue and green halves. On the blue side, a brown hand with a white shirt and blue cuff gives a thumbs-down gesture, while on the green side, a similar hand gives a thumbs-up. The text "Vote on proposal" is shown above this graphic. At 0:01, the circular graphic changes to an orange background, displaying a white document with grey and blue text, representing a "Bill presented to Parliament" as indicated by the text above the circle. The timeline marker continues to advance. By 0:02, the circle's background turns light blue/teal, and three stylized head-and-shoulder figures appear within it: a dark-skinned man in a white shirt and black tie, a light-skinned woman with red hair in a blue dotted top, and a dark-skinned man in a white shirt and orange tie. Flanking this central circle are two groups of seated, stylized figures on what appear to be parliamentary benches – red benches on the left and green benches on the right – representing members of parliament. The text "Bill is shaped" is displayed above the central graphic, signifying the stage where the bill is debated and amended. The timeline marker continues its forward progression throughout this sequence.

The video segment begins with a solid orange background featuring four diverse, smiling, flat-design cartoon people in the bottom right corner. This quickly expands to a line of eight diverse cartoon people across the bottom of the screen, representing "The voting PUBLIC," a phrase that appears in black text above them, connected by dotted lines. The background then transitions to light purple, and the initial group slides away, replaced by four figures depicting historical changes in voting rights: a medieval king, a man from the 17th or 18th century, a suffragette holding a sign that reads "Votes for Women," and a modern woman. The scene then shifts to a green and teal map of the UK and Europe. Seven new diverse cartoon people, each wearing an electoral ribbon of a different color (green, red, purple), appear at the bottom, and a large brown hand points down at them from the top of the screen, symbolizing the act of voting for elected representatives.

The video segment opens with a light-skinned hand using a pen to mark an 'X' in a square on a white sheet of paper labeled "Ballot paper" (English) against a yellow background. This transitions to four diverse, animated candidates with different colored hair and skin tones standing on pedestals of varying heights, each wearing a rosette, implying election winners, against a teal background. Next, a light-skinned person with yellow hair is shown with thought bubbles and question marks, then a ballot paper with an 'X' appears in the thought bubble, indicating confusion about who to vote for. Following this, a blue diagonal line slices through a campaign poster featuring a smiling male candidate with dark hair, labeled "Vote" (English) and "A. Candidate" (English). The scene shifts to the candidate in a grey suit handing out a small "Vote" (English) flyer with his face to two diverse individuals. Then, two candidates are shown debating, one saying "Explain?" (English) in a speech bubble. Another scene shows a male candidate talking to two people, one of whom greets him with "Hi there!" (English). A television screen with "Channel 1" (English) and the same male candidate's smiling face is displayed. This is followed by a browser window showing a candidate's image and "Our Policies" (English) with a list, with the word "Manifesto" (English) appearing below and then circling around the browser window, emphasizing the concept. The video then shows a smiling male candidate in a suit with a grey rosette, standing with a diverse group of supporters on his left, and a smaller, different group of diverse people on his right, against a teal background. The scene changes to a brown background, showing a diverse group of five candidates with various colored rosettes standing in front of a dark door with the number "10" (English) and a white fanlight above it, referencing 10 Downing Street. Then, another blonde-haired candidate in a green suit joins them. Subsequently, a larger, more diverse group of candidates, including some from the first group and new faces, all wearing different colored rosettes, are shown together in front of the same door, suggesting a broader government or coalition. The screen then changes to a teal background with a pink ribbon folding to spell "YOUR VOICE" (English) in yellow text. Finally, a dark-skinned hand in a teal sleeve inserts a marked "Ballot paper" (English) into a black ballot box, and colorful swirls emanate from the box, signifying the act of voting.

The video begins with a green wavy badge featuring the white number "18" on a purple background, then transforms into an animated registration form on a teal background with fields for "User" (with a person icon) and "E" (with an envelope icon), and a "REGISTER" button which is clicked by a mouse cursor. An orange background appears with various speech bubbles representing public concerns: "New jobs for us," "Student loans," "Local hospitals," "Climate change," "My school," and "Our pensions." A diverse group of flat-design cartoon people stand below these bubbles, with "Student loans" and "My school" then highlighted. The scene shifts to a man in a suit (MP) at a desk, then standing before the Houses of Parliament, where a hand holding a megaphone displays the text "We want change" (English). A hand interacts with a smartphone on a light pink background, tapping on profiles labeled "Baroness" and "Lord" from "www.parliament.uk" (English). Three circular icons then illustrate communication methods: a hand writing on paper labeled "Write" (English), a hand holding a phone with "CALL" (English) on the screen labeled "Call" (English), and a laptop displaying an email interface labeled "Email" (English). On a teal background, a central yellow circle labeled "Youth party" (English) connects to various profile cards with cartoon faces, showing a network. A browser window with a "Petition" (English) form is shown, where a cursor clicks a "SEND" (English) button. On a pink background, a central black circle rotates through topics like "The environment," "Jobs and wages," "Schools and hospitals," and "Global issues" (all English), surrounded by diverse cartoon people. A split screen shows groups of people, with some wearing rosettes, and speech bubbles stating "Support our cause" (English), while another woman holds a sign saying "We want change" (English), before merging into one scene on a teal background. A yellow circle with chat bubbles inside appears on a red background, with a pink banner below stating "Student Council" (English). The video concludes with a bright green screen showing a pink banner with "SUMMARY" (English), followed by an animation on a teal background of the Houses of Parliament, and three circles appearing one by one: the first showing people in a chamber with "Debating big issues" (English), the second showing a document labeled "Law" with "Making and shaping laws" (English), and the third showing people around a table with "Holding government to account" (English), ending with a hand marking an "X" on a ballot paper.

The video opens on a bright yellow background with black text reading "What will you do?" displayed above a magenta banner that contains white text "www.parliament.uk/get-involved". This encourages viewers to get involved with Parliament. A few seconds later, a yellow circular animation rapidly expands from the center, covering the banner and text entirely, transitioning the scene to a plain white background. Finally, the logo for the "PARLIAMENT EDUCATION SERVICE" appears in teal, featuring the word "PARLIAMENT" in a small square with an ornate crest on the left, and "EDUCATION SERVICE" written in larger letters to its right.
